title: Sweeper: Security Evidence & RBAC v2 Procedures
content:
Purpose:
This runbook ("Sweeper") defines a compact, operational set of checks and templates to validate security posture for any planned deployment that touches customer data, RBAC v2 role changes, audit-log schema changes, or SIEM export adjustments. It is intended to be used by release engineers, SREs, and the security reviewer on call.

Scope and when to use:
- Use Sweeper for feature or infra changes that modify: RBAC policies or role bindings; audit log fields or retention; log export destinations (SIEM/ELK/Kinesis); automation that produces compliance evidence.
- Not for purely UI text updates or non-production experiments.

Quick read checklist (operators):
1) RBAC v2 sanity (required):
   - Confirm new roles follow least-privilege naming and are scoped to a team namespace or entitlement group.
   - Each role must have an associated justification paragraph (2-3 sentences) in PR description.
   - Confirm there are no wildcard permissions ("*" verbs/resources) introduced.
   - Verify role binding TTLs for temporary elevated access; if none, require justification for permanent binding.
   - Verify approval chain: role author -> team lead -> sec-reviewer. Add JIRA key to role PR.

2) Audit log schema changes (required if any log fields are added/renamed):
   - Add an entry to the audit-log-schema.md (include field name, type, example value, and privacy classification).
   - Backfill plan: if a field is renamed, include migration strategy and sample migration script location.
   - Confirm that Personally Identifiable Information (PII) is not logged in plaintext. If PII is required, mark field as "redacted" and document KMS/HSM encryption used.

3) SIEM export and evidence automation (required if export changes):
   - Validate destination ACLs and that export credentials are stored in KMS.
   - Confirm SIEM field mappings and an example event (see sample below).
   - Run local evidence export job against a staging snapshot and attach resulting artifact to the PR.

4) Exception approvals (if any control is intentionally bypassed):
   - Fill the Exception Request template (section below).
   - Must include risk summary, mitigations, TTL, compensating controls, and business justification.
   - Security leadership must approve exceptions > 72 hours.

5) Sign-off items before merge:
   - PR has linked JIRA ticket (SEC- or ENG- prefix).
   - Automated tests for RBAC enforcement exist and pass in CI.
   - Evidence export run produced artifact uploaded to attached artifacts in JIRA.
   - Reviewer checklist completed (security reviewer, SRE, product owner).

RBAC v2 procedural details:
- Role naming convention: team.feature.privilege (example: serving-runtime.cache.read).
- Role granularity guidance: prefer multiple narrowly-scoped roles that can be composed by binding rather than large monolith roles.
- Temporary elevation: all temporary bindings must be issued via the ephemeral-access system (ticketed) and have a TTL <= 72 hours unless approved. Include link to ticket in PR description.
- Automated validation script: /infra/tools/rbac-validator runs against PR; failures are blocking. Provide remediation snippets in PR comments.

Audit log schema example (add to schema registry):
- Field checklist: name | type | sample | privacy
  - event_time | ISO8601 | 2025-11-12T15:02:17Z | public
  - actor_id | string | user:ashapatel | internal
  - actor_role | string | serving-runtime.cache.read | internal
  - action | enum | role_binding.create | internal
  - resource | string | infra/serving-runtime/cluster-12 | internal
  - request_id | uuid | 3f8b2a10-... | public
  - outcome | enum | success | public
  - raw_payload_hash | sha256 | a3f1... | internal
  - pii_masked | boolean | true | internal

Sample audit event (stringified JSON example to include in schema docs):
{"event_time":"2025-11-12T15:02:17Z","actor_id":"user:ashapatel","actor_role":"serving-runtime.cache.read","action":"role_binding.create","resource":"infra/serving-runtime/cluster-12","request_id":"3f8b2a10-6b9e-4d2f-a0f1-9c45d3b2f6aa","outcome":"success","raw_payload_hash":"a3f1b9...","pii_masked":true} 

SIEM export mapping (operational notes):
- The SIEM connector expects flattened event fields. We map audit fields to siem_* prefixes: siem_time, siem_actor, siem_action, siem_resource, siem_request_id, siem_outcome.
- Use the ingestion schema version header: X-SIEM-Schema: aud-1.2.
- Example SIEM sample (CSV/PSV acceptable) is generated by automation job sweep-evidence/exporter: see /infra/automation/sweep-evidence/README.md.
- Retention: exported events to SIEM must follow retention policy sec:siem-retention (default 365 days for audit, 90 days for raw payloads).

Evidence automation run procedure (minimal run):
1) From your local workstation (with VPN): 
   - git checkout <pr-branch>
   - ./infra/automation/sweep-evidence/run --staging-snapshot --include-logs --output=artifact.tar.gz
2) Validate artifact: tar tzf artifact.tar.gz && head -n 200 artifact/audit-events.ndjson
3) Upload artifact to JIRA ticket via --jira-key flag or to secure share (link must be included in PR).
4) Automation produces a compact manifest (artifact.manifest.json) that lists counts, schema versions, and SHA256 checksums. Attach manifest to the ticket.

Exception approval template (paste into JIRA when requesting):
- Summary: short description of exception and affected systems.
- Risk: bullet list of what could go wrong (data exposure, elevated access).
- Mitigations: compensating controls and monitoring (E.g., stricter alerting, 24h guard).
- TTL: timestamp or duration after which the exception expires.
- Approvers required: security-manager, eng-lead, product-ops.
- Evidence: attached outputs from sweep-evidence job and troubleshooting logs.

Sign-off template (copy into PR description at time of request):
- Security reviewer: [name] (link to review comment)
- SRE reviewer: [name]
- Product owner: [name]
- Evidence artifact: [link to artifact.tar.gz or manifest]
- RBAC validator result: [pass/fail and link to run]
- Exception attached: [yes/no and link] 

Post-deploy monitoring and rollback triggers:
- Post-deploy watch window: 24h for RBAC or log-schema changes, 72h for SIEM destination changes.
- Automatic rollback triggers: repeated "unauthorized" spikes > 0.5% of traffic for 15 minutes, SIEM export failures > 5% for 10 minutes, key-mismatch errors, or unexpected PII ingestion detected by content-scan rule.
- On trigger: follow incident runbook (link: confluence:SEC-INCIDENT-RUNBOOK), escalate to on-call sec and sprint SREs, consider immediate rollback to prior deployment.

Notes and common pitfalls observed historically:
- People often add fields to audit logs for debugging without considering privacy; always run the content-scan locally before PR.
- Role names that include team member usernames create churn; prefer stable team prefixes.
- SIEM field mismatches are the top source of post-deploy noise — include a sample event in the PR to speed validation.

Appendix: quick commands and helpers
- rbac validator: infra/tools/rbac-validator --pr=1234
- evidence run: infra/automation/sweep-evidence/run --staging-snapshot --output=artifact.tar.gz
- check siem mapping: infra/tools/siem-validate --schema aud-1.2 artifact/audit-events.ndjson

If you are the security reviewer receiving this package: prioritize RBAC checks first, then audit schema, then evidence artifact sanity. If anything is unclear ping #sec-review on Slack and add a short note to the PR summarizing the gap.

Revision history:
- 2025-11-12 created by Asha Patel (initial draft)
- 2025-11-14 updated: added SIEM mapping and automation manifest guidance (Ivy Soto)

End of Sweeper runbook.
